findings.reason: The protected Python solution finds the shortest distance between word1 and word2 by making a single pass over wordsDict, maintaining the latest indices latest1 and latest2. Upon encountering either word, it updates the corresponding index and evaluates abs(latest1 - latest2). The algorithm runs in O(n) time and O(1) space; no candidate is required.
Scanning wordsDict linearly and tracking the most recent index of each target word guarantees that all candidate adjacent pairs (where one is the latest occurrence relative to the other) are checked.

A single linear pass over n words in wordsDict performs O(1) string comparisons and index distance calculations per word, yielding O(n) total time. Auxiliary space is O(1) for scalar index trackers. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Accepts wordsDict (List[str]), word1 (str), and word2 (str), returning the integer minimum distance between word1 and word2.

The approach accurately details single-pass latest-occurrence tracking, distance minimization logic, and O(n) time / O(1) space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover storing all index lists space trade-offs, all-pairs comparison quadratic costs, adjacent target minimum distance behavior, repeated word occurrences, and distinct word match safety.
